definition.alternative: Agents fail to form unassigned objectives, collapsing into purely extrinsic reward maximization.
assumptions: Environments with high state-space complexity provide sufficient uncertainty to support curiosity-driven objective formation.
Standard multi-objective reinforcement learning frameworks are capable of integrating intrinsic motivation signals.
definition.falsification: If agents consistently converge solely to the provided extrinsic reward function without deviation into behavior patterns associated with information gain or curiosity under controlled entropy, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Autonomous goal formation in agents occurs when curiosity-driven intrinsic motivation mechanisms are optimized alongside extrinsic rewards, allowing the emergence of objectives not explicitly defined in the initial reward function, observable through refined novelty metrics under high entropy conditions.
definition.uncertainty: It remains unclear whether intrinsic motivation functions necessarily lead to stable, non-trivial goal emergence or if they collapse back into simple noise-seeking behaviors.
